questions.q: What is the fundamental difference between a view and a stored procedure?
options: A view saves one SELECT statement; a stored procedure saves an entire script (multiple statements, variables, logic)
There is no real difference — they are interchangeable terms
A stored procedure can only contain a single SELECT, unlike a view
Views can be executed with EXEC; procedures cannot
questions.explain: This is the core distinction — a procedure bundles anything covered in this chapter, not just a query.

questions.q: How do you run a stored procedure once it's created?
options: EXEC procedure_name; (or the full word EXECUTE)
SELECT * FROM procedure_name;
RUN procedure_name;
CALL procedure_name();
questions.explain: EXEC is the T-SQL way to invoke a stored procedure's entire body as a single call.

questions.q: What does the usp_ prefix convention indicate?
options: A common (optional) naming convention for 'user stored procedure,' mirroring the vw_ convention for views
It's required syntax for CREATE PROCEDURE to work
It marks a procedure as read-only
It's a reserved system prefix that cannot be used by developers
questions.explain: Like vw_ for views, usp_ is a naming habit this course uses consistently, not a hard requirement.

questions.q: Can a stored procedure's body contain IF/ELSE, loops, and variables?
options: Yes — that's the whole point of a procedure versus a view, which can only hold a single SELECT
No, procedures can only contain SELECT statements, same as views
Only IF/ELSE is allowed, not loops
Only if SCHEMABINDING is specified
questions.explain: The usp_ProductCatalogSize example demonstrates DECLARE, SELECT-assignment, and IF/ELSE all inside one procedure.

questions.q: What does ALTER PROCEDURE do, compared to DROP PROCEDURE?
options: ALTER PROCEDURE redefines an existing procedure's body; DROP PROCEDURE removes it permanently
They do the same thing — remove the procedure
ALTER PROCEDURE only works on views, not procedures
DROP PROCEDURE renames the procedure instead of deleting it
questions.explain: This mirrors the ALTER VIEW / DROP VIEW pattern from Lesson 58, applied to procedures.
